Instead, he strips photography to its essential materiality, and presents photographs that reveal physical actions on the surface of the light-sensitive paper. This gallery rotation is divided into two parts. Opening in February, Breuer will present selections of old and new works; then in mid-March, he will reorganize the gallery into a space that resembles a darkroom, emphasizing the artist’s process of creating a picture.

Title: Desire and Deliverance: Drama in the Old Testament
Description:
To coincide with the Science Museum of Minnesota's exhibition on the Dead Sea Scrolls, the MIA presents "Desire and Deliverance: Drama in the Old Testament," an exploration of how artists transformed biblical narratives of Noah, Jonah, Susanna, and others into scenes of passion, morality, piety, and nationalistic pride.

Each of the featured artists—Jasper Johns, Ellsworth Kelly, Roy Lichtenstein, Frank Stella, and Andy Warhol—has left a unique and indelible mark on the development of contemporary art and printmaking during the second half of the twentieth century. Title: Rembrandt in America
Description: During the Gilded Age, Americans developed an appetite for paintings by 17th-century Dutch master Rembrandt van Rijn. His paintings are now found in public and private collections from coast to coast. This exhibition will bring together one of the most substantial groups of Rembrandt paintings assembled in America in a generation. Description: This exhibition brings together works by modern and contemporary female artists that exhibit innovative approaches to the vessel in various media. The department of Decorative Arts, Textiles, and Sculpture conceived Basins, Baskets, and Bowls around a group of significant recent acquisitions in ceramic, fiber, and wood. Title: Masks from the West-African Dan People
Department: Art of Africa and the Americas
Description:
Masks are the most important art form of the Dan, who live on either side of the border between Liberia and Côte d'Ivoire. This installation includes about 10 masks, from the MIA and from two local collectors. The exhibition's purpose is twofold: to show the variety of forms of Dan masks, and to highlight the diversity of their functions.

Title: Cover Story: Master Bookbindings from the Collection
Description: A beautiful display of decorative bindings by noted French, Belgian, English, and American artists and designers. Most are from the golden age of fine binding, 1920–1960, but with John Graham’s sensational cover for Picasso’s illustrated edition of Balzac’s Chef d’oeuvre inconnu we see the shift to a new era exemplified by the work of Anselm Kiefer and Jim Dine.

Title: Robert Bergman: Portraits, 1986-1995
Beware Her Wiles: Woman as Temptress in the Renaissance Tradition
Description: Women will discover how to keep their men in line, and gentlemen will realize that regardless of their strengths, they are inevitably outmatched. Let the great women of old—Judith, Delilah, Salome, and their sisters—teach you a thing or two about the Power of Women.

Title: Embarrassment of Riches: Picturing Global Wealth, 2000-2010
Description:
Embarrassment of Riches explores how contemporary media artists have depicted wealth over the last ten years and upends the usual attention given to images of poverty. Following a decade of unprecedented historical fluctuations of wealth on a global scale, this exhibition is not a celebration of affluence and consumerism but an examination of the societal effects of prosperity.

Description:
The fine and tenacious threads that represent generational and societal memory are the foundation for the work of this Minnesota artist.
Bojagi, a traditional Korean art form, inspires eun-Kyung Suh’s work. Bojagi are cloths wrapped around objects for protection and transport. Although these were made out of small scraps of material, woman would decorate them to create beautifully patch-worked wrappers. Suh uses this technique to protect memories and experiences. Title: Kuon (Eternal Flow of Time): Mayumi Amada
Description:
The fine and tenacious threads that represent generational and societal memory are the foundation for the work of this Minnesota artist.
Mayumi Amada’s exhibition “Kuon: Eternal Flow of Time” focuses on domestic and feminine roles, including and the role woman play in creating continuity and home. Description: Hayter’s Atelier 17 was seminal for the adventurous printmaking of the mid-20th century. He encouraged artists to try their hand at printmaking, and the studio became a meeting place for the exchange of artistic ideas. Hayter’s stimulus was particularly widespread, for Atelier 17’s 60-year run in Paris (1927 to 1988) was interrupted by a ten-year exile in New York during the 1940s. Title: New Pictures 3: James Welling, Glass House
Description: New Pictures 3 will feature James Welling's innovative photographs of Philip Johnson's modernist architectural masterpiece, Glass House (1949), as well as other select works that explore the refraction of light. Welling, a Professor of Photography at the University of California, Los Angeles, uses colored filters to capture the luminous effects of Johnson's glass-skinned house during different times and changing lighting conditions. New Pictures 3 will be on view from August 19, 2010 through Apr

Title: Chairevolution! 300 Years of Designing the Chair
Description: What do we mean when we say “good design”? Do we know it when we see it? When we sit on it? This exhibition takes a look at the meaning of good design though the examination of just one form over the course of more than 300 years – the chair. From the basic Tudor to Phillippe Starck’s Louis Ghost Armchair for Kartell, we will explore in just twenty-one chairs how designers over time have reconciled the desire for design with the basic need to find a place to sit. This exhibition is held in conju

Title: Wide-Eyed: Panoramic Photographs
Description: The word “panorama” was coined in the late eighteenth century by the Irish artist Robert Barker to describe his own elongated paintings.  Shortly after the invention of photography, in 1839, its practitioners also embraced the format, first making multiple-part pictures and, later on, individual images created with a succession of panoramic cameras. Each individual has their own story, but these stories are made unique by our surroundings both natural and man-made and by the burden of what we hide and what we hope to present. Jennifer Davis, Erika Olson, Terrance Payne, and Joe Sinness create work that focuses on self-image and the desire to create order where nature would have it otherwise.

Title: Bad to the Bone: Prints from the Grip of Death
Description: Death has a lot on his calendar. Of course, there is the work of ministering to and menacing his endless stream of more or less willing clients. But, he also has parties to attend, concerts to perform, and places to go. He is an athlete, adept at riding horses, driving chariots, and maneuvering other contraptions that most of us know little about. Title: From Press to Page: Book Arts in Minnesota
Description:
This exhibition highlights the creativity and craftsmanship of some of Minnesota's leading contemporary book artists and fine presses. 
Minnesota enjoys a national reputation as a locus for the book arts. Indeed, the metropolitan area of Minneapolis and St. Paul is frequently ranked behind only New York as a hotbed of book arts activity. Description: Photographers, naturally, have a unique relationship with the camera, given it is their tool of choice. They are accustomed to being behind it, shooting with it, and seeing the results of their efforts. Many photographers are also comfortable situating themselves in front of their lenses, making self portraiture either an aspect of their work or its mainstay. Title: Hot House: Flowers for after the Frost
Description: On view from the Equinox nearly until the Solstice, this floral free-for-all will include works from every department in the museum. As in any greenhouse, we can expect harmony and discord... abundant brilliant blossoms and a few that faltered. From Redouté to Warhol, Mondriaan [That’s no typo—he used two A’s in his early days] to Mapplethorpe, this will be a mixed bouquet. Tom Rassieur is not known for his green thumb, but he’s going to turn up the heat and hope for the best.

Title: Venice on Paper
Description: As a maritime power at the heart of international trade and travel, Venice has been an important cultural center since the Middle Ages, inspiring both native and visiting artists to create exceptional and unprecedented works of art. Described as the "Queen of the Adriatic" with its maze of canals and confluence of Byzantine, Arab, and European architecture, Venice has also been a favorite subject for artists as they have strived to capture the city's unique character and beauty. From Renaissance

Title: Saints and Sinners: Women in Renaissance Prints
Description:
Women in the Bible and in legends about saints were depicted frequently in Renaissance art to portray contemporary ideas about the ideal woman, almost invariably by male artists. In this exhibition, 22 prints are examined from a feminist perspective, stressing the woman’s subservient role in 15th and 16th century Europe, but also the negative perception of women as immoral temptresses. In some examples, the overt moralistic message is tempered with erotic overtones. 
The works in this exhibitio

Title: The Genius of Martin Schongauer: The Engravings
Description: This exhibition features twenty-two engravings by Martin Schongauer (about 1450–1490), the most influential German artist of the fifteenth century. Drawn from the museum’s permanent collection, this selection of rare prints demonstrates the exceptional quality, innovative technique, and renowned refinement of Schongauer’s work.

Title: Visions of Piety: Devotional Prints in the Counter-Reformation
Description: This focused exhibition of prints examines the dramatic religious imagery produced in Catholic Europe in this period, and the power of print to foster private devotion and promote tenets of the Church.

Title: Wild Things
Description: Satyrs—half man, half goat. Centaurs—half man, half horse. Tritons—half-man, half-fish. They and their female counterparts are known to cavort in the woods and wreak havoc on the seas. Yet they also have their civilized side—raising families, attending parties, playing music, worshiping, and even providing artistic inspiration. So, in the interest of survival, we survey images of composite creatures from the Renaissance, the Baroque, and the Rococo eras of art.

Title: William Blake: Illustrations of The Book of Job
Description:
The British visionary poet, painter, illustrator, and engraver William Blake (1757-1827) was one of the leading figures of the Romantic era. Illustrations of The Book of Job, first published in London in 1825, ranks among Blake's best-known and most enduring achievements. This masterwork of the engraver's art comprises 21 line engravings and an engraved title page; each plate is accompanied by text that Blake selected from Job and other books of the Bible.
The Book of Job, one of the books of t

Title: L’Ancien Régime: Life at the French Court in the 17th and 18th Centuries
Description: The glittering society of Versailles was a popular subject in prints in 17th and 18th-century France. For the estimated 1,000 courtiers who kept rooms at the chateau, a dizzying schedule of amusements was offered each season—fêtes, masquerade balls, outdoor theater performances and concerts, fireworks displays—with no expense spared. Arranging these entertainments and parties was important business, overseen by an official bureaucratic department of the king’s household—called the Menus Plaisirs

Title: From Rembrandt to Matisse: Selected Works on Paper
Description: This exhibition presents more than 60 outstanding European and American prints and drawings, from the seventeenth to the twentieth century, featuring works by Rembrandt, Goya, Pissarro, Denis, and Matisse. Drawn primarily from the MIA’s permanent collection, the selection will highlight recent acquisitions and important loans.

Title: From Dürer to Picasso: Selections from the Department of Prints and Drawings
Sir Francis Seymour Haden: Physician and Printmaker
Description: During his lifetime, Sir Francis Seymour Haden (1818-1910) was better known as a surgeon than as an artist. It was considered proper for a 19th century English gentleman to learn how to draw and to collect art, but more as an avocation than as a profession. Haden pursued his medical training in London and Paris and eventually came to specialize in obstetrics. His private practice was successful enough to allow him to acquire a significant collection of old master prints, a well-appointed London

Title: Metamorphosis: Maria Sibylla Merian's Insects of Suriname
Description: In 1699, Maria Sibylla Merian (1647-1717) sailed to Suriname to draw and study the insects of the rain forest. She was particularly fascinated by the transformation of caterpillars into butterflies and moths, and her images reveal their successive stages of development from egg, to caterpillar and pupa, and finally to mature adult. Title: On the Same Page: Artist's Books New to the Collection
Description:
Artist’s books emerged as an art form in the late nineteenth century, and have since become repositories for unbounded artistic imagination. The chance to interpret a favorite text with their own vision is, for many artists, irresistible. The artist’s books exhibited here—spanning more than a century—display a unique commingling of words and picture on the same page, from Pierre Bonnard’s exquisitely daring Parallèlement to Donald Baechler’s quizzical Double Whammy. 
The Minneapolis Institute o

Title: Edward Ruscha: Stains
Description: One of the most innovative and influential artists to emerge in the 1960s, veteran Los Angeles painter Ed Ruscha is internationally known for his irreverent and often ironic depictions of Southern California culture, architecture, and urban environment. A first-generation Pop artist who explored meaning in the objects and circumstances of everyday life, Ruscha consistently established a strong conceptual framework for his art. His life-long fascination with words and language—especially the inte

Title: The Pose of Poetry and Prose: Aristide Maillol Interprets the Artist's Book
Description: French sculptor Aristide Maillol (1861-1944) extended his modeling genius to the art of book illustration. This exhibition, drawn entirely from the museum's permanent collection, features a nearly complete survey of Maillol's artist's book oeuvre, with texts ranging from Virgil to Paul Verlaine.

Title: Pablo Picasso: Livres d'Artistes
Description: Internationally celebrated as a painter and sculptor, Pablo Picasso (1881-1973) was also an innovative and prolific printmaker and book artist. His extensive graphic oeuvre includes more than twenty-five livres d’artistes, deluxe limited edition illustrated books featuring original prints. Drawn entirely from the MIA’s permanent collection, this exhibition showcases a selection of more than a dozen of Picasso’s livres d’artistes, with texts ranging from Buffon to Tzara.

Title: Breaking with Convention: Avant-garde Artist's Books
Extraordinary Editions: Artist's Books of the 20th Century, Part I and II
Description: This two-part exhibition presents a selection of outstanding twentieth-century artist’s books drawn from the MIA’s permanent collection. The works on display embody unparalleled artistic achievement among the many modern and contemporary artists who were and are active in the book arts including Hans Arp, Fernand Leger, Max Ernst, Man Ray, Matisse, Picasso to name only a few.

Title: Marks of Intention: Abstract Art on Paper 1945-2005
Description: This installation features a selection of more than fifty drawings, prints, and artists’ books that demonstrates the persistent interest in abstraction and non-objective art among modern and contemporary artists working in the postwar era. The works on view were drawn entirely from the museum’s permanent collection and range from Jackson Pollack’s rare early experimental etchings to Robert Motherwell’s dynamic gestural color prints to Brice Marden’s monochromatic minimalist abstractions. The ins

Title: The 1960s: Prints and Editions
Description: 45 original prints and edited artist’s books by many of the decade’s foremost artists are drawn from the MIA’s permanent collection.

Title: From Life: Figural Art on Paper, 1980-2006
Description: This exhibition of prints, drawings, and artist’s books explores some of the many artistic approaches and ideas of contemporary artists employed in the depiction of the human form. The present selection, featuring work by more than thirty-five contemporary artists, includes recent acquisitions not previously exhibited in the MIA’s galleries.

Title: Space/Surface: Contemporary Sculptors as Printmakers
Description: Contemporary artists have long embraced a multi-disciplinary approach in their artistic practice. This exhibition showcases editioned prints by more than twenty leading sculptors, including works by Richard Serra, Louise Bourgeois, Lee Bontecou, Ellsworth Kelly, Frank Stella, Sol LeWitt, Donald Judd, Joel Shapiro, Kiki Smith, and Martin Puryear.

This exhibition features a selection of more than 50 prints, monotypes, and multiples by leading American and European artists of the second half of the 20th-century, including Robert Rauschenberg, Jasper Johns, Helen Frankenthaler, Cy Twombly, Robert Motherwell, Chuck Close, Joan Mitch

Title: The Artful Animal: 500 Years of Beasts, Birds, and Other Earthly Creatures
Description: Drawn primarily from the MIA’s permanent collection, this inter-departmental exhibition examined the theme of the animal in art from the 16th century to the present. Approximately 80 prints, drawings, watercolors, paintings, sculptures, books, and decorative objects, which depict mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, fish, insects, and imaginary creatures, were featured.

Description: In 1889, a group of young artists banded together in Paris and called themselves the Nabis, from the Hebrew word for “prophets.” Included in this group were Pierre Bonnard, Edouard Vuillard, Paul Ranson, Paul Sérusier, Maurice Denis, Félix Vallotton, Ker-Xavier Roussel, and Aristide Maillol. They sought to integrate art with life and move beyond what they perceived as the limits of Impressionism. Title: A Vision of Paris: Etchings of Charles Meryon
Description: The etchings of Charles Meryon (1821-1879) reveal a vision of Paris before the changes put into effect during the rule of Napoleon III's Second Empire. Meryon's prints capture the essence of the medieval sections of town that were being torn down to accommodate the wide boulevards and new parks and squares of the Emperor's master plan. Title: At the Water's Edge: 19th-Century Prints from the Jones Collection
Description: This installation will survey the way water provided powerful inspiration to a variety of gifted 19th-century artists. From the canals of Venice to the busy rivers of the Thames and the Seine, from sailing ships to fishing boats, water proved an irresistible subject in the works of James McNeill Whistler, Francis Seymour Haden, D.Y. Cameron and others.

Title: The Prints of Francisco Goya
Albrecht Dürer and the Prints of the Danube School
Description: This exhibition highlighted the artists of the Danube School who lived and worked by the Danube River from Regensburg to Vienna in the early 16th-century. The prints of the Danube School are characterized by a profound sensitivity to nature. Landscape and atmospheric elements were used to an unprecedented degree to emphasize subject and mood, while the structure of growing, organic things governed the compositions. Description: This exhibition contains approximately 25 masterpieces created before 1600 from the Department of Prints and Drawings. The majority of the works have been added to the collection since 1985 and showcase the beauty of European printmaking of the 15th and 16th centuries.

Title: Monsters and Mayhem: Renaissance Prints from the Jones Collection
Description: This installation takes an unusual look at 15th century prints devoted to real and imagined beasts, fierce battles, bawdy mischief makers, and general bad behavior of the worst kind. It will feature works by many of the most important artists of the period including Andrea Mantegna, Israhel van Meckenem, Albrecht Dürer, and Martin Schongauer.

Description: Mannerism, a refined artistic style originating in Italy, took hold in Flanders in the 16th century, bringing with it a new repertoire of subjects, techniques, and sensibilities. It coincided with the rapid development of printmaking, especially engraving, by Flemish artists. A Book of Hours is a lay person's prayer book read during private devotions. These books were small enough to be held in the hand, and were easily portable. Description:
The Minneapolis Institute of Arts has actively collected drawings for nearly a century, acquiring works of outstanding quality by many of the world’s most prominent artists. Expanding on this curatorial imperative, the Department of Prints and Drawings has in recent years redoubled its efforts to collect important contemporary drawings by both established and emerging artists.

The irresistible tensions on the surfaces of her large-scale paintings keep viewers looking. Description: The scientific method is a process for documenting events, creating knowledge, and testing theories. Peter Happel Christian measures, collects information, and records data, creating sculptures and photographs that are positioned at the intersection of art, science, and history. He observes the technologies that mediate our everyday relationship with art and natural phenomena, including geography, cartography, and topographical surveys. Title: Beauty and Power: Renaissance and Baroque Bronzes from the Peter Marino Collection
Description: Over the course of more than two decades, the well-known New York architect Peter Marino has formed an exemplary collection of highly important Italian and French bronze sculptures of the Renaissance and the Baroque. This exhibition features approximately 30 of his European bronze sculptures from the golden age of this artistic genre. This exhibition showcases the premier wood art collection of Minneapolitans David and Ruth Waterbury, which is considered one of the best in the country. The Waterburys have embraced the evolution of the field and its artists for twenty-five years, collecting pieces that range from exquisitely turned bowls, to objects conceived around irregularities within the material, to works that explore imaginative ways to manipulate the medium.

Description: Joseph F. McCrindle (1923–2008) was a tireless and gifted art collector, with a particular fondness for drawings. He began collecting seriously in the 1960s and never stopped, forming one of the greatest private collections of drawings in America in the 20th century.
